description: Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a beloved Indian dish featuring succulent chicken pieces simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Its mild spice profile and luxurious texture make it a global favorite, perfect for a comforting and satisfying meal. Enjoy this restaurant-style classic in the comfort of your home.

ingredients.notes: made from soaked cashews or blanched whole cashews

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, a pinch of salt, and lemon juice. Mix thoroughly to coat the chicken. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 7-10 minutes. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Makhani Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons unsalted butter and 1 tablespoon vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté until the onions turn translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Sauce
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes, remaining 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until the tomato mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides of the pan. Stir in the cashew paste and 1/4 cup water, simmering for another 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods from the sauce base. Let the mixture cool slightly, then carefully transfer it to a blender. Blend until the sauce is completely smooth and creamy. For an exceptionally silky sauce, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on the solids to extract all liquid.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth sauce in the pan. Add the sugar or honey, the remaining 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, and the crushed kasuri methi. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and cook for just 1-2 minutes more, ensuring the sauce does not boil after adding the cream. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the cooked chicken pieces slightly under a broiler or on a grill before adding them to the sauce.
Using good quality canned crushed tomatoes or ripe fresh tomatoes is crucial for the authentic flavor of the makhani sauce. Always blend until perfectly smooth.
Always add cream at the very end of cooking and do not boil the sauce vigorously after its addition to prevent curdling and maintain its smooth texture.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is a dish that needs little introduction. It’s a global phenomenon, celebrated for its rich, creamy texture and a flavor profile that perfectly balances sweet, savory, and a hint of tang. Originating from the bustling kitchens of Delhi, this iconic curry has become a staple in Indian restaurants worldwide and a beloved choice for a hearty, satisfying lunch. If you’ve ever craved a dish that feels like a warm, comforting embrace, Butter Chicken is undoubtedly it. This article will guide you through understanding, preparing, and perfecting this exquisite Indian classic right in your own kitchen.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, where chefs Kundan Lal Jaggi and Kundan Lal Gujral experimented with leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato and butter-based gravy. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained popularity across India and eventually, the world.

At its core, Butter Chicken is characterized by tender pieces of chicken (often marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried) swimming in a velvety smooth, subtly sweet, and mildly spiced tomato-cream sauce. The "butter" in its name isn't just a suggestion; it's a foundational ingredient, contributing significantly to the dish's luxurious mouthfeel and flavor. Kashmiri chili powder often lends a vibrant red-orange hue without excessive heat, making it approachable for most palates. The addition of cream, cashews, and a touch of sugar or honey balances the acidity of the tomatoes, creating an unforgettable symphony of flavors that makes it an ideal, indulgent Indian lunch recipe.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting an authentic Butter Chicken requires a combination of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices. Here’s what you’ll need:

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (or more!)
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped (optional, for deeper flavor)
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water for 30 minutes
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1-2 tablespoons sugar or honey (to taste)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Butter Chicken Recipe

Making Butter Chicken from scratch is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a truly delicious result:

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. You can also grill or bake the chicken for a more authentic tandoor-like flavor. Set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base**
In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. If using, add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the pureed or crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have cooked down and the oil starts to separate.

**Step 4: Add Spices and Cashews**
Drain the soaked cashews and blend them with a little water to form a smooth paste. Add the Kashmiri chili powder, cumin, coriander, and turmeric to the tomato mixture. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Stir in the cashew paste and cook for another 2-3 minutes.

**Step 5: Simmer and Blend**
Add about 1/2 to 1 cup of water to the sauce, bringing it to a simmer. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove from heat and carefully transfer the sauce to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky sauce, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve.

**Step 6: Finish with Butter and Cream**
Return the smooth sauce to the pan. Stir in the garam masala and crushed kasoori methi. Add the heavy cream and a generous knob of butter. Stir until the butter is melted and the sauce is heated through. Add sugar or honey to taste; this helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes and enhances the overall flavor. Adjust salt as needed.

**Step 7: Combine Chicken and Sauce**
Gently fold the cooked chicken pieces into the creamy sauce. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the Murgh Makhani sauce.

**Step 8: Garnish and Serve**
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Your homemade Butter Chicken is now ready to be enjoyed!

## Tips for the Best Homemade Butter Chicken

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavorful and tender it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality butter and ripe, flavorful tomatoes. Kashmiri chili powder is crucial for color without excessive heat.
*   **Smooth Sauce:** Blending the sauce thoroughly and potentially straining it ensures that velvety restaurant-quality texture.
*   **Balance Flavors:** The beauty of Murgh Makhani lies in its balance. Taste and adjust the sugar, salt, and acidity (lemon juice can be added at the end if needed) until it’s perfect for your palate.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** Don't skip the kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves). Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils; they impart a unique, essential flavor to Butter Chicken.
*   **Resting Time:** Like many curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen and meld.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a perfect Indian lunch.

*   **Naan or Roti:** The classic pairing. The soft, fluffy bread is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or a fragrant jeera (cumin) rice provides a neutral base that complements the curry's robust flavors.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon and cilantro) adds a refreshing contrast and cuts through the richness.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt dip, such as cucumber raita, can offer a pleasant counterpoint to the subtle spices.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is a masterpiece, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary preferences or availability of ingredients.

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Easily transform this into Paneer Makhani by substituting chicken with cubed paneer (Indian cheese). Tofu or mixed vegetables (like peas, carrots, and potatoes) can also be used for a delicious vegetarian version.
*   **Healthier Options:** To reduce calories, use less butter and cream. You can substitute some of the heavy cream with plain Greek yogurt (stirred in at the very end to prevent curdling) or even a cashew-almond milk blend. Baking or air-frying the chicken instead of pan-frying also reduces oil.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, use a spicier variety of chili powder or add a fresh green chili to the sauce.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain the sauce's thickness and richness, you can use a tablespoon of poppy seeds or ground melon seeds, or simply cook the tomato base down longer until it thickens naturally.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic tandoori smoke, once the Butter Chicken is cooked, create a small well in the center, place a small heat-proof bowl with a burning piece of charcoal, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Its creamy texture, fragrant spices, and tender chicken make it an irresistible choice for any occasion, especially as a comforting and satisfying lunch. Don't be intimidated by the ingredient list; the process is straightforward and the delicious reward is well worth the effort. Dive into the world of Indian cuisine and create this timeless classic in your own kitchen!
